pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to The Hawthorns School | Independent Prep School & Nursery in Surrey
pageCache.text:
A school for life
Welcome to The Hawthorns, a thriving independent nursery and day prep school for girls and boys aged 6 months to 13 years in Bletchingley, Surrey.
In a warm, family atmosphere, we give each child every opportunity to realise their potential through academic achievement and by engaging in activities which build their confidence. We wish to fuel each child’s enthusiasm for life and encourage them to engage with the world they live in.
September 2026 marks 100 years of Hawthorns. As we celebrate our centenary, we look forward to the next chapter of our story as part of the award-winning Caterham Family of Schools.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wraparound Care and Clubs - Hawthorns Prep School & Nursery
pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care and Clubs
We know busy parents need flexibility, so during term time we offer school wraparound care from 7.15am to 6.00pm.
Mornings
A nutritious breakfast is served from 7.15am, giving children a calm, settled start to the day.
Afternoons
After lessons, we encourage children to get outside and make the most of the fresh air, whether that's through one of our 30-plus extra-curricular activities or our after-school care, with collection any time up to 6.00pm.
For younger children, after-school care feels like a home from home. We prioritise outdoor play whenever weather allows, with children free to run around and let off steam, alongside time to play with friends, chat about their day, and relax. Indoor space is also available for quieter moments, and if a child would rather unwind with a book, that's just as welcome. A hot tea is provided for children up to and including Year 4.
As children move up the school, the choice grows further, with plenty of active, extra-curricular options such as team practice for the sport of the season, roller-skating, judo and fencing, alongside supervised homework sessions for Years 5 to 8.
Booking
Spaces are booked through our online system, with the flexibility to reserve a place termly or as a one-off, right up to the evening before. There's space for everyone.
Full pricing details are available here. We accept childcare vouchers.
School Holidays
Our holiday provision runs 50 weeks of the year for children in Reception to Year 8. Find out more about Camp Hawthorns here.

pageCache.pageTitle: A camping adventure for our Explorers - Hawthorns Prep School & Nursery
pageCache.text:
A camping adventure for our Explorers
After a busy week exploring the theme of 'Camping holidays', our Nursery Explorers enjoyed an adventure of their very own!
A tent was set up for the children to explore, providing the perfect setting for stories and imaginative play. Explorers took turns to climb into the camping chairs and read books, while the sandpit became a seaside-inspired sensory experience, filled with shells and starfish shapes to discover.
After all that exploring, there was only one thing left to do: have a little camp-out themselves! Our Explorers took their afternoon nap outdoors, enjoying a peaceful rest after a busy week of learning and adventure.
At Hawthorns Nursery, every day brings new opportunities to explore, imagine and discover. Open year-round for children from 6 months to 4 years, our Nursery is a place where little minds grow, curious hearts flourish and learning begins with adventure.

pageCache.text:
OHA Personal Development Fund
The Old Hawthornian Assosiation has recently launched the Personal Development Fund which offers financial assistance (up to £1,000) to a maximum of two Old Hawthornian pupils each year. The Personal Development Fund will help to fund voluntary or enterprising projects or ventures which will support their personal growth or development during their ‘A’ level years and to the year following university”. eg helping to fund voluntary work overseas, training etc.
In return those pupils will become OHA ambassadors by giving presentations to current pupils and staff and providing information and photos for case studies to be used in mailings for pupils, Old Hawthornians, the OH Facebook site and The Hawthorns website.
Since its launch ten grants have been awarded to Old Hawthornians. Find out more about their experiences below.
Applications should be received by 1st April each year, to be put to a vote at the AGM. However, we shall also consider applications at other times. Download the Old Hawthornian Personal Development Fund application form.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Upper School (ages 11-13) - Hawthorns Prep School & Nursery
pageCache.text:
The Upper School (ages 11-13)
Years 7 & 8 at The Hawthorns School are a time of opportunity and responsibility. Aged 11 to 13, our Upper School pupils set the tone of the School: they lead, rather than follow the example of older teenagers.
As the oldest members of the School, Upper School pupils take on roles of responsibility becoming prefects, House Captains, heads of a sport or drama and take leading roles in our orchestra and choirs, as well as being part of our top sports teams playing regular fixtures. The Upper School is also a time of service, with pupils supporting younger children develop their reading, running 'fix-it' IT workshops, helping organise indoor activities during 'wet' breaktimes and watching over younger children in the dinner queue. Self-esteem flourishes and you can see their confidence in debating, the camaraderie that builds up in sports teams and the development of their independent study skills. It is the most wonderful time in their young lives, to be at the top of the tree, to draw breath before moving into a much more demanding and competitive adult world at senior school.
“A school where childhood still seems to last the right length of time.” Current parent
In a warm, nurturing environment, these children are given the opportunity to grow up before the full impact of adolescence, two crucial years in which to live in a child’s world before being pulled into a world of young adults. During breaktime, our Upper School children are just as likely to be found climbing trees in our woodland, as playing manhunt across our glorious 35 acres. Mobile phones are not permitted in school.
Our pupils thrive on the challenge of a vigorous, broad, varied and stimulating curriculum that prepares them not just for their senior school but life beyond. Pupils continue to be taught by specialist teachers in a broad range of subjects including Maths, English, Science, Computing, French, Spanish, Latin, Sport, Art, Music, Drama and Design & Technology. They complete their own ‘mini EPQ’, a version of the much-respected Extended Project Qualification taken by many sixth formers. As well as a Form Teacher, Upper School pupils are supported by a tutor and given the tools to approach their learning in an exciting and organised manner. A rich programme of exciting residential trips both at home and abroad encourages self-belief and independence.
We welcome a number of new pupils into Year 7 and with strong ties to over 20 of the top senior schools in the south-east, our team of Senior School Guides are ready to support families choosing the right senior school for their child.

Drama
Drama aims to foster a love of performance in all forms, to inspire the children in a creative environment. Thinking something does not make it true. Wanting something does not make it real. Enjoying something makes it worthwhile!
Drama can help children learn about emotions, problem solving, and relating to other people. Through their experiences with drama, children develop their imaginations and their confidence. One of the most special things about creative drama is that there are no "wrong" answers.
There is a strong tradition of drama at The Hawthorns. In the Nursery through to Year 2 drama is an integral part of the curriculum, with role-play being an important element in Topic work. We prepare several productions and each child from Year 2 to Year 8 has a drama lesson once a week. Throughout the year children of all ages are given the opportunity to perform. Our aim is for every child to enjoy taking part.

Governors
The Hawthorns School is a charitable trust and is overseen by a Board of Governors who serve the School as volunteers with experience from a wide variety of professions, including independent and maintained sector education. Responsible for the oversight of the performance of the School and the safeguarding and welfare of all children, Governors play an active part in school life visiting, observing lessons and examining performance, setting fees and meeting staff and parents.
The Board is led by the Chair of Governors, Mr David Chalmers, who may be contacted through the School Office.

Maths
Maths at The Hawthorns is intended to prepare students for an ‘Education for Life’ by ensuring they have secure knowledge and core fundamental skills which are developed in the Early Years through to the Upper part of the School. Its cross-curricular nature ignites creativity, continuity and mastery in all attainment areas of the subject. Our bespoke syllabus which commences from the Early Year Foundation Stages through to Key Stage 3 delivers independent learning and fosters growth mind-set in learners of all abilities.
The Parent and Pupil Workshops, Maths Road Shows, Junior Maths Challenges and the Virtual Learning Platforms seek opportunities to stimulate, inspire and develop resilient learners; this also ensures that learners experience the subject in a variety of enjoyable and challenging contexts.
Close collaboration with other Prep Schools and Senior Schools ensures that good practice is shared and implemented which provides personalised learning to each pupil.

Music
Music is carried in the heart of every child; it is our job to unlock it. We provide an outlet for emotion and a tool for communication that enables children to fully experience life. Our musicians not only practise teamwork but also hone their confidence to stand up on their own and be different. We prepare children for a bright future, learning to give things a go, to persevere and to reflect on the next steps with recognition of the courage and toil required to succeed. We value choice and encourage every child to engage at their level, searching to find the right instrument at the right time.
In a snapshot we enjoy musical games in the Rainbow nursery, explore the instruments of the orchestra in Year 3, rehearse weekly as a class ensemble from Year 4 and compose film music and pop songs in the Upper School. We embrace cross curricular links through study of musical history and world music.
For those wanting more, we offer a mini string players scheme from the Ark, shared lessons from Year 1 and individual music lessons from Year 2 leading to a wealth of opportunities with something for everyone. Your child will have the opportunity to choose between the six choirs, at least five different instrumental ensembles, six steel bands and a number of guitar ensembles. We regularly share our music forging links with the local community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral Care - Hawthorns Prep School & Nursery
pageCache.text:
Pastoral Care
The highest levels of Pastoral Care lie at the heart of The Hawthorns’ community. Guided by our motto ‘Love God, Love thy Neighbour’, we provide a nurturing and stimulating environment in which each individual girl and boy feels happy and valued, and develops a progressively fuller understanding of themselves and others.
We follow a wholly inclusive approach, with all staff embracing the fact that in partnership with parents and carers, we have a direct responsibility for the well-being of the children entrusted to our care. More specifically, our dedicated and experienced pastoral and welfare teams provide specialist support at all levels, from Early Years through to Year 8.
Expectations of positive behaviour, including good manners and friendship, and of learning from challenges and mistakes as much as from successes, are made clear and reinforced from the earliest age. A wealth of opportunities and experiences exists both inside and outside the classroom to enable Hawthorns children to develop in these ways: opportunities and experiences such as participating in a teamwork day; being a member of one of our House ‘families’, within which older pupils take responsibility for younger ones; showing prospective parents around the School; discussing citizenship within a PHSEE lesson; having the chance to lead as one of our a variety of School Officers.
By the time children are ready to leave us, they have gained from having had the time, space and caring support to grow into independent, healthy and confident individuals with a clear sense of right and wrong, and of their future place in the world around them.
"The Hawthorns has transformed life for my daughter. Her confidence was at an all-time low, at only 5 years old she felt inferior to her peers, having been told by her teachers at her old school that she was not as able as her friends. Her form teacher scooped her up and within a week was sending her home with books to read - something she had never experienced before and absolutely delighted her! With the gentle care, kindness, support and encouragement The Hawthorns has given, she has blossomed, growing her confidence, social skills and academic abilities."
"There has not been a single day that my daughter hasn’t come home from The Hawthorns with a spring in her step and a smile on her face, she has absolutely loved her time with you."

Science
At The Hawthorns, we want every child to become excited and engaged in learning about science. We see science as an essential part of understanding the world around us. We want to allow our pupils to develop their knowledge of the natural world, hone their experimental skills in the chemistry lab, and carry out investigations into physics topics such as forces, electric circuits and sound.
This interest is encouraged by our experienced and enthusiastic teaching staff. We have two modern Science labs which our older pupils come to for specialist teaching. Our younger pupils also have their own Lower School science room which allows them to carry out experiments in a well-equipped space.
A regular programme of trips and activities enhance the classroom learning and allow the pupils to see how Science fits into the real world.
With a recognised shortage of scientists in the world today, we hope that by ‘lighting the spark’ as early as possible, maybe one day Hawthorns pupils will go on to become doctors, astronomers, zoologists, engineers, chemists or maybe even science teachers!

Welcome from the Registrar
As the mother of two children who attended The Hawthorns, I have seen first-hand how pupils benefit from the huge range of opportunities that they are given here. My children thrived in this nurturing, family environment, developing confidence and kindness, and growing into well-rounded individuals, both now thoroughly enjoying and achieving at their senior schools. My experience as a parent at the School gives me a unique insight which I believe will help you to get to know the School better throughout the admissions process.
I understand that choosing the right school for your child is a huge decision, but my job is to make the process as easy and reassuring as possible. Please don’t hesitate to get in touch with any questions at all, however small or insignificant they may seem.
To arrange a visit please contact me on 01883 743048 ext 2019, by email on admissions@hawthorns.com or use our online booking form.
I look forward to meeting you and your family and showing you around our wonderful school.
Debbie Kingerlee, Registrar

pageCache.pageTitle: The Curriculum - Hawthorns Prep School & Nursery
pageCache.text:
The Curriculum
The Hawthorns seeks to develop a love of learning. The Early Years Foundation Stage Curriculum builds upon the natural curiosity evident in the Early Years, developing confidence, questioning and independent thinking.
Curiosity about the world is fostered through diverse opportunities in and out of the classroom and through expert teaching. Each transfer, from year to year, is thoughtfully managed. Special Needs and Able Child Co-ordinators oversee the progress of every child. With a focus on English and Maths and a curriculum based on The Hawthorns Compass Curriculum a truly broad and balanced curriculum is experienced.
The School is innovative and forward thinking, embracing current educational change and forging ahead with the use of new technologies. Progression and continuity are measured through tracking systems, with standardised testing forming just a part of this process in order that learning is central to each child’s success.

The Hawthorns Nursery FAQs
What age can my child start at The Hawthorns Nursery?
The Hawthorns Nursery offers full day, year-round nursery provision to children aged six months to four years. Discoverers, Explorers and Adventurers are housed in Little Thorns, our purpose-built nursery, completed in September 2023. Pioneers and Ark Pre-School are housed in our unique boat shaped building with its gorgeous Secret Garden. Find our more here.
What are the opening times for The Hawthorns Nursery?
The Hawthorns Nursery is open for adventure from 7.15am to 6.00pm, 50 weeks of the year.
Do you offer term-time provision as well as year-round provision?
Yes! Upon Registration, families may choose between 50 weeks of provision a year and term-time provision. There are three terms in a year and they are delivered in line with The Hawthorns School terms, dates for which can be found here.

What is the minimum number of session required?
We ask that children at The Hawthorns Nursery to do a minimum of four sessions a week. This can be any combination of Full Days, School Days, Mornings and Afternoon sessions. A 'Full Day' and a 'School Day' both count as two sessions.
Do you offer school length days at The Hawthorns Nursery?
We understand that some families may wish to pick their nursery aged children up at the same time as their older siblings and offer the flexibility of a 'School Day' option from 8.00am to 4.15pm.
When is The Hawthorns Nursery closed?

Closure dates are published a year in advance and are available here.

How will I know what my child has been up to during the day?
Our partnership with you as parents is essential, as we aim to create a wider family structure for your child. At the end of each day, you’ll be met by your key person and they will run you through all the activities and exciting developments of the day.
Through an app available on your smartphone, we will provide updates on events in your child’s day, such as when their nappy was changed, what they’ve eaten and their nap times. We’ll also post pictures and videos regularly to your news feed so that your whole family can see what they’ve been up to!
We are also able to share your child’s learning journal, our observations of their wellbeing, learning and development through the different experiences they are having, and link these to the early years foundation stage so that you can see and understand the progress your child is making and the next steps they are working towards.
"I am particularly pleased with the communication and updates provided through the Famly app. It has been a valuable tool for us to stay connected with my son's daily activities and progress. This transparency has been reassuring and greatly appreciated."
How do you settle children into the Nursery?
"We have nothing but praise for you and your whole team. My son has settled so well and we really appreciate how understanding everyone was during the first week of wobbles."
Do you offer Funded Early Education?
The Hawthorns School and Nursery offer up to fifteen hours of funded early education per week, for up to 38 weeks a year, for three- and four-year-old children, only. This funding is a universal offer and is available to all children from the term after their third birthday. Children can continue to receive this funding in Reception at The Hawthorns School, until they reach statutory school age, which is the term after their fifth birthday.

Nursery
Welcoming a new baby is an exciting time for any family. As a father of three, I understand how truly special those first years are as we watch our children's day-to-day development and celebrate all their 'first' moments.
I also appreciate just how busy modern life can be, which is why we are delighted to offer our Nursery with full-day, year-round provision for children aged 6 months to 4 years.
As parents, we all want the best for our children. In line with our whole school philosophy, our vibrant and nurturing environment provides opportunities for your child to thrive and flourish, developing their personality and character whilst growing intellectually, emotionally and physically.
The Hawthorns has a real family feel. From your child's first day, we prioritise the development of secure, strong relationships with our nursery staff, so that your child feels loved and cared for, settles in quickly and grows in confidence and independence.
Our fully qualified team have the skills and expertise to provide the very best start for your child. More than that, they are passionate about Early Years education, committed to creating a caring and stimulating environment where curiosity is encouraged and learning is tailored to support each stage of development, from baby to toddler, toddler to pre-schooler, and pre-schooler into 'big' school, in our Reception classes.
Located on our school site, our Nursery benefits from our extensive grounds, woodland areas and facilities, making each day rich with possibilities and providing a wonderful start to your child's educational journey.
I warmly invite you to contact our Registrar, Debbie Kingerlee, for further information or to arrange a visit. I look forward to meeting you and your family soon.
